title: Lags, Rolling Windows & Leakage
interviewAnswer: Lag and rolling features summarize past information, but they must be constructed using only data available at prediction time. Centered windows or post-outcome aggregates silently leak the future.
keyPoints: Use the same pipeline in backtests and production.
why: Lags, Rolling Windows & Leakage appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Lag and rolling features summarize past information, but they must be constructed using only data available at prediction time. Centered windows or post-outcome aggregates silently leak the future. Feature availability timestamp matters. Use the same pipeline in backtests and production. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Predict tomorrow’s demand using demand up to today, never a 7-day centered moving average that includes tomorrow.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Lags, Rolling Windows & Leakage make?
How would you validate or debug Lags, Rolling Windows & Leakage in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
